summary.text:
Sales sheet
Four copies of Mina’s name must change together.

Separate tables
One customer row changes. Her orders still carry ID 1.
The outlines mark four places to edit in the sales sheet and one in customers. Updating only one sheet row would give Mina different current names on different lines.

Sales sheet
No order line exists for Edda, so there is nowhere to put her.

Separate tables
Customer 3 exists without any order referring to her.
A line-shaped row cannot record just a customer. Inventing an order to hold Edda’s name would record a purchase that never happened.

Sales sheet
The only row carrying Tariq’s name would disappear.

Separate tables
Order 102 goes; customer 2 remains.
The crossed-out row is the sales sheet’s only record of Tariq. With separate tables, removing an order does not remove the independent fact that Tariq is a customer.
